items.reason: The definition of C itself. Rewritten from 'Set C = R^2' with coordinate arithmetic to the stem field R[x]/(x^2+1) with the real embedding and imaginary unit i, which is the construction the page's own Kronecker and simple-extension apparatus builds. Dependencies change from [def-real-numbers] to the polynomial-ring and simple-extension definitions at order 54 and below.

That C is a field. Rewritten to follow from the irreducible-quotient route (x^2+1 is irreducible over R, so R[x]/(x^2+1) is a field) together with uniqueness of the a+bi representation from the power basis, rather than from a direct inverse formula over R^2.
Conjugation, real and imaginary parts, and modulus. Statement text is unchanged; its dependency set changes because it now rests on the quotient model rather than on the coordinate definition.

The load-bearing case. As published, proof step 2.1 is [given] and reads 'The Euclidean norm triangle inequality on R^2 is exactly |z+w| <= |z| + |w|', carried entirely by def-p-norms-on-rn and lem-p-norms-are-norms-and-induce-the-published-metrics at order 167 — a forward reference no legal form of relocation can remove. The rewrite derives the triangle inequality from Lagrange's identity (a^2+b^2)(u^2+v^2) - (au+bv)^2 = (av-bu)^2 >= 0 and squaring monotonicity, whose inputs sit at order <= 9. Two order-54 items need this lemma (thm-real-automorphisms-of-the-complex-numbers, thm-every-complex-number-has-a-square-root), so leaving it at 189 would reintroduce the very forward reference this change exists to remove.
